can include manufacturing, supply chain, human resources. These modules are integrated together and are able to access the same data and execute complex business processes. Today, Cloud-based accounting information systems are increasingly popular for both SMEs and large organizations for lower costs. With adoption of accounting information systems, many businesses have removed low skills, transactional and operational accounting roles. AIS typically follow a multitier architecture separating the presentation to the user, application processing and data management in distinct layers. The presentation layer manages how the information is displayed to and viewed by functional users of the system (through mobile devices, web browsers or client application). The entire system is backed by a centralized database that stores all of the data. This can include transactional data generated from the core business processes (purchasing, inventory, and accounting) or static, master data that is referenced when processing data (employee and customer account records and configuration settings). As transactions occur, the data is collected from the business events and stored into the system’s database where it can be retrieved and processed into information that is useful for making decisions. The application layer retrieves the raw data held in the database layer, processes it based

is useful for making decisions. The application layer retrieves the raw data held in the database layer, processes it based on the configured business logic and passes it onto the presentation layer to display to the users. For example, consider the accounts payable department when processing an invoice. With an accounting information system, an accounts payable clerk enters the invoice, provided by a vendor, into the system where it is then stored in the database. When goods from the vendor are received, a receipt is created and also entered into the AIS. Before the accounts payable department pays the vendor, the system’s application processing tier performs a three-way matching where it automatically matches the amounts on the invoice against the amounts on the receipt and the initial purchase order. Once the match is complete, an email is sent to an accounts payable manager for approval. From here a voucher can be created and the vendor can ultimately be paid. MEANING OF ACCOUNTING INFORMATION SYSTEMS An accounting information system (AIS) is a structure that a business uses to collect, store, manage, process, retrieve and report its financial data so that it can be used by accountants, consultants, business analysts, managers, chief financial officers (CFOs), auditors and regulatory and tax agencies. 21.4 COMPONENTS OF AN ACCOUNTING INFORMATION SYSTEM Accounting information systems generally consist of six main parts: people, procedures and instructions, data, software, information technology infrastructure and internal controls. 1. People The people in AIS are simply the system users. Professionals who may need to use an organization’s AIS include accountants, consultants, business analysts, managers, chief financial officers and auditors. AIS help the different departments within a company work together. For example, management can establish sales goals for which staff can then order the appropriate amount of inventory. The inventory order notifies the accounting department of a new payable. When sales are made, sales people can enter customer orders, accounting can invoice customers, the warehouse can assemble the order, the shipping department can send it off, and the accounting department gets notified of a new receivable. The customer service department can then track customer shipments and the system can create sales

notified of a new receivable. The customer service department can then track customer shipments and the system can create sales reports for management. Managers can also see inventory costs, shipping costs, manufacturing costs and so on. 2. Procedure and Instructions The procedure and instructions of AIS are the methods it uses for collecting, storing, retrieving and processing data. These methods will be both manual and automated, and the data can come from both internal sources (e.g., employees) and external sources (e.g., customers’ online orders). Procedures and instructions will be coded into AIS software; they should also be “coded” into employees through documentation and training. Procedures and instructions must be followed consistently to be effective. 3. Data The data contained in AIS is all the financial information pertinent to the organization’s business practices. Any business data that impacts the company’s finances should [PAGE 599] Unit 21: Accounting and Financial Information System Page 583 of 596 NOTES Accounting for Managers Uttarakhand Open University go into AIS. The data included in AIS will depend on the nature of the business, but it may consist of the following: (a) sales orders (b) customer billing statements (c) sales analysis reports (d) purchase requisitions (e) vendor

consist of the following: (a) sales orders (b) customer billing statements (c) sales analysis reports (d) purchase requisitions (e) vendor invoices (f) check registers (g) general ledger (h) inventory data (i) payroll information (j) timekeeping (k) tax information This data can then be used to prepare accounting statements and reports such as accounts receivable aging, depreciation/amortization schedules, trial balance, profit and loss, and so on. Having all this data in one place - in the AIS - facilitates a business’s recordkeeping, reporting, analysis, auditing and decision-making activities. For the data to be useful, it must be complete, correct and relevant. 4. Software The software component of AIS is the computer programs used to store, retrieve, process and analyze the company’s financial data. PROCUREMENT & PURCHASE APPROVAL POLICY Document Version: 1.0 Effective Date: 01 January 2025 Applicable System: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) System Department Owner: Finance & Procurement 1. Purpose This document defines the procurement and purchase approval process followed within the ERP system of mpinext Manufacturing Pvt. Ltd. The objective of this policy is to ensure controlled purchasing, financial accountability, and compliance with internal audit requirements. All procurement activities must be initiated, approved, and recorded through the ERP system. 2. Scope This policy applies to all employees involved in procurement-related activities, including: Purchase requisition creation Purchase approval and authorization Purchase order generation Invoice verification and payment processing Manual purchases or offline approvals outside the ERP system are strictly prohibited unless explicitly approved as an exception. 3. Roles and Responsibilities Role Responsibilities and ERP Permissions Employee Create purchase requisitions in the ERP system Department Manager Approve purchase requisitions up to ₹50,000 Finance Manager Approve purchase requisitions above ₹50,000 Procurement Officer Convert approved requisitions into Purchase Orders Accounts Team Verify invoices and process payments Each role is assigned system permissions within the ERP to ensure segregation of duties. 4. Purchase Requisition and Approval Workflow [PAGE 2] The procurement

system permissions within the ERP to ensure segregation of duties. 4. Purchase Requisition and Approval Workflow [PAGE 2] The procurement workflow within the ERP system follows these steps: 1. An employee raises a Purchase Requisition in the ERP system with required details such as item description, quantity, and justification. 2. The requisition is automatically routed to the respective Department Manager for approval. 3. If the requisition value exceeds ₹50,000, it is forwarded to the Finance Manager for additional approval. 4. Upon approval, the Procurement Officer generates a Purchase Order (PO) in the ERP system. 5. The Purchase Order is issued to the selected vendor through the ERP system. No purchase shall be made without an approved Purchase Order. 5. Invoice Processing and Payment Invoice processing is handled through the ERP system as follows: 1. Vendors submit invoices referencing the corresponding Purchase Order number. 2. The Accounts Team performs a three-way match between: Purchase Order Goods Receipt Note Vendor Invoice 3. Any discrepancies are flagged in the ERP system for review. 4. Once verified, invoices are approved for payment and scheduled as per payment terms. Invoices without valid Purchase Orders will not be processed. 6. Escalation Rules The ERP system enforces

as per payment terms. Invoices without valid Purchase Orders will not be processed. 6. Escalation Rules The ERP system enforces the following escalation rules: Purchase requisitions pending approval for more than 3 working days are automatically escalated to the next approval authority. Rejected requisitions must include a rejection reason in the ERP system. Emergency or urgent purchases require Finance Manager approval irrespective of purchase value. 7. Compliance and Audit [PAGE 3] All procurement transactions are logged within the ERP system and are subject to internal and external audits. Audit logs must be retained for a minimum period of 5 years. Any deviation from this policy will be treated as a compliance violation. Procurement activities conducted outside the ERP system may result in disciplinary action. 8. Insight to find data quality issues, validate how data relationships comply with standards, and to monitor, measure, and improve the quality of your data. Data Insight shows the return on investment of quality data, and the impact of poor data on the business. Therefore, it’s a valuable tool when you’re considering the purchase of technology. Use Data Insight to: Gain a high-level view of the quality of your data Drill into your data to view quality scores for tables and columns View a sample of the data that doesn’t pass your rules Monitor trends in your data quality over time Data Insight projects Each deployment of SAP Information Steward supports multiple users in one or more Data Insight projects. A Data Insight project is a collaborative workspace for data stewards and data analysts to assess and monitor the data quality of a specific domain and for a specific purpose. For example, for customer quality assessment, sales system migration, and master data quality monitoring. Administrators create and define Data Insight projects. Administrators can create many projects in Data Insight. However, there’s one default project that is included with Data Insight named Enterprise Project. Administrators create projects and grant permissions in the

one default project that is included with Data Insight named Enterprise Project. Administrators create projects and grant permissions in the Central Management Console (CMC). For complete information about creating projects, setting permissions, and creating connections, refer to the Administrator Guide. Data Insight always opens to the Projects page first. The software lists all projects to which the user has permissions, plus the Enterprise Project. Sort projects by name or creation date using the Sort projects by option. Select the applicable project to continue with tasks in Data Insight.  Note The default Enterprise Project is always listed first, regardless of the sort selection. Cache indicates whether the software reads the data from the source and loads it into memory or pageable cache. Caching a source increases performance only when the data source is used as the right table portion of a join. Caching does not affect the join ranking. The following table describes the caching options for joins. Cache option Affects on processing Yes Enables source caching. Processing is more efficient be­ cause caching limits the number of times the system must access the database. Disables caching. Processing is less efficient because the source is not cached into memory. Automatic The software determines the caching behavior. Tables are al­ ways cached when the Automatic cache option is set. The default cache option is Automatic. When choosing to cache a source, ensure that you have sufficient memory or pageable cache. Content types add an additional dimension to your data by providing meaning. Content types categorize your data based on data type and the content of the column. Data Insight provides predefined content types, such as name, firm, phone, date, and address. You can create custom content types that Data Insight includes in suggestions from a content type profile. You can accept the suggested content type or enter your own content type based on the profile results.  Example A column named

the suggested content type or enter your own content type based on the profile results.  Example A column named Contact_Info includes data such as e-mail, phone, or address. After a content type profile, look at the profiling results for the number and percent of records that appear to be e-mail, phone, or address data. Use the number and percent data to decide to accept or reject the suggested content type. Content Type profiling uses custom logic such as proximity to other fields, patterns, and so on, to provide a content type that gives meaning to your data. Content types are useful when defining rules and having rules automatically suggested after profiling.  Note Columns with BLOB, CLOB, and Long data types can’t be assigned a content type. Data Insight becomes better at assigning your custom content types, and learns to correlate other data with similar characteristics with the custom content type.  Restriction Before Data Insight automatically suggests the custom content types for other tables, run a column profiling task with the Median & Distribution option selected. Otherwise, Data Insight doesn't auto- associate columns to this content type for other tables. After you accept the suggested custom content type

Insight doesn't auto- associate columns to this content type for other tables. After you accept the suggested custom content type for one table, Data Insight “learns” to associate the data type to the content type.  Example You created a content type named Reward Number and assigned it to a column that has numeric data in the format 9-777-51912. Then you run a content type profile task on a table that has a numeric column with the n-nnn-nnnnn pattern. Data Insight suggests the Reward Number content type for the numeric column with the matching pattern, and you accept the suggestion. You notice that a small percentage of columns for which Data Insight suggested the Reward Number content type are actually columns that contain Social Security numbers. The pattern in the Social Security column is similar to the Reward Number, but not the same. Therefore, you investigate the problem and adjust your data, to prevent the mistake. You now have better trust in the accuracy of your data. The content type profiling helped improve your data quality. Table level quality scores When Information Steward generates a table level quality score, it determines the score on all rules applied to all columns of the table. Data Insight Connections 3.10.8.7.1 Include source with failed data When you use tables that are created from portions of multiple tables, it’s difficult to determine the main source for a column. To associate the source for failed data, choose to include the source when you create the rule task. Data Insight then outputs both the failed data and the source data to the SAP Information Steward repository for the failed data connection. The source data enhances your ability to filter and drill down into the failed records to gain more insight into data problems.  Note To enable the Include Source option, choose a failed data connection from the dropdown list in the Define Task: Rule dialog box.  Note For more information about failed data connections and permissions that your administrator makes in the Central Management Console, see Failed data connection and permissions [page 176]. When the source table has a primary key, including the source data also enhances the trending capability of Data Insight. Data Insight tracks date and time information whenever the source data changes. Also, with a set primary key, Data Insight can perform delta loads on the second and subsequent runs of the task. a set primary key, Data Insight can perform delta loads on the second and subsequent runs of the task. Consider setting a primary key in your source data in the following ways: Use the applicable DBMS to access the data table and set a primary key. After you set a primary key, reimport the table to SAP Information Steward before rerunning rule tasks. Create a new Information Steward view in Data Insight and include the source table. the software assigns a group ID and fails the entire data set. The two functions ensure uniqueness: is_data_dependent: Checks the data dependencies between primary and dependent columns. is_unique: Checks the uniqueness of a column or a set of columns The software groups the records from the source in the failed data table and assigns a unique group ID using the following syntax: ruleID_col1ID_col2ID...._seq# Where: ruleID: The rule that caused the rows to fail col#ID: The column to which the rule is bound. There can be more than one column. seq#: The identifier that separates the rows based on their value. Data Insight assigns multiple group IDs under the following circumstances: When a rule is bound to the same table, but with different columns When different rules are bound to the same table with the same columns When different rules are bound to the same table with different columns  Note Performance can be affected (slower) in concurrency situations. The following table contains the terminology that we use in the Cleanse Results pages. 250 PUBLIC User Guide Data Insight [PAGE 251] Term Definition Cleansed Data, such as person, title, firm, phone, e-mail, data, and So­ cial Security Number (SSN), is listed as cleansed for one of the following reasons: The data has problems that the software is able to cor­ rect. The data is correct on input and needs no corrections. Corrected address The address has problems that the software

rect. The data is correct on input and needs no corrections. Corrected address The address has problems that the software is able to cor­ rect. Invalid The data contains errors that the software can't correct. Suspect Data, such as person, title, firm, phone, email, date, and SSN, is listed as suspect for one of the following reasons: The data is potentially invalid, such as a person name field that contains data that appears to be an organiza­ tion name. The data is incomplete, such as a phone number with too few numbers. The data includes extraneous data, such as an SSN field that includes text in addition to the SSN. The data is of low confidence, such as a first name field populated with the word Sunshine. It could be a name, but the software can’t determine with high confidence that it’s a name. Valid address The address is correct on input and needs no corrections. The following table contains the terminology that we use in the Match Results pages of Data Cleansing Advisor. Term Definition Confidence The certainty of a match based on the similarity of the re­ cords. High-confidence matches:

Cleansing Advisor. Term Definition Confidence The certainty of a match based on the similarity of the re­ cords. High-confidence matches: Records that are exactly alike or have a high probability of similarity. Medium-confidence matches: Records that are similar enough to be considered matches, but review them to be sure because something about the match is ques­ tionable. Low-confidence matches: Records that are groups of three or more records in which there exists an indirect match. Review the matching records to ensure that the results are as intended. Indirect match A pair of records in the same match group that don’t match. An indirect match occurs when records match by associa­ tion. For example: Record A matches record B. Record B matches record C. Consequently, Data Cleansing Advisor places record A and record C in the same match group even though they don’t match directly. Match A pair or group of records that Data Cleansing Advisor finds to be potential duplicates. Match group A collection of records that consist of a master record and one or more subordinate records that Data Cleansing Advi­ sor finds to match each other. In the data view, Data Cleansing Advisor lists match groups by group

Cleansing Advi­ sor finds to match each other. In the data view, Data Cleansing Advisor lists match groups by group ID. The group ID itself isn’t meaningful; it’s just a way to identify the match group. Near match Records that don’t match but are close to meeting the crite­ ria for being a match. There are two categories of near matches: Records that nearly match a match group Records that nearly match other near matches Nonmatch Records that don’t match other records. Nonmatching re­ cords include the subcategories of near matches and uniques. User Guide Data Insight PUBLIC 287 [PAGE 288] Term Definition Strictness The extent to which records must match to be considered matches: Loose match strictness: A lower percentage of similar­ ity. Tight match strictness: A higher percentage of similar­ ity. Unique Records that don’t match or even nearly match other re­ cords. Unique records are a subcategory of nonmatching re­ cords. The formula for calculating the scorecard is fairly straightforward: The rule bindings for a rule are calculated and combined to equal the score for the rule. The scores for the rules are combined to equal the score

and combined to equal the score for the rule. The scores for the rules are combined to equal the score for the quality dimension. The scores for the quality dimensions are combined to equal the key data domain (KDD) score. The weight for each object group must total 100%.  Note If you assign a weight of zero to an item, the item (including its children) doesn't appear and isn't used in any calculations in the scorecard view. 330 PUBLIC User Guide Data Insight [PAGE 331] Information Steward calculates the scorecard score and saves it in the local repository using the Calculate Scorecard utility. Administrators schedule the Calculate Scorecard utility in the Central Management Console (CMC). By default, the Calculate Scorecard utility runs daily, but your administrator can change the frequency in the CMC. Also, a rule task calculates the scores for rule bindings. Rule tasks calculate the scores for all rules bound to tables, flat files, and views. For example, M may be taken to mean either

resolution) Sometimes a parsed value may have more than one meaning. For example, M may be taken to mean either medium or meter; cream may be a color, a dairy product, or the formulation of a pharmaceutical or cosmetic product. In these cases, depending on usage, you may want to assign a parsed value to more than one attribute. Often you can accomplish that by defining the context in which the parsed value would occur. For example, if M is preceded by a number, then it means meter. Cleansing Package Builder can assign parsed values to more than one attribute as long as context has been defined for all but one alternative; if your data contains two alternatives, you must define context for at least one of them, if your data contains three alternatives, you must define context for at least two of them and so on. A conflict occurs when you have assigned a parsed value to one attribute and then attempt to assign the same parsed value to a second attribute. You can resolve a conflict in one of several ways: Define a context. Specify an adjacent attribute that consistently precedes the attribute to which you want to

of several ways: Define a context. Specify an adjacent attribute that consistently precedes the attribute to which you want to assign the conflicting parsed value. Specify an adjacent attribute that consistently follows the attribute to which you want to assign the conflicting parsed value. In effect, when a conflict occurs, specifying an adjacent attribute creates an if-then statement. If the adjacent attribute precedes, then the if-then statement says: IF attribute A precedes, THEN assign the parsed value to User Guide Cleansing Package Builder PUBLIC 829 [PAGE 830] attribute B. If the adjacent attribute follows, then the if-then statement says: IF attribute A follows, THEN assign the parsed value to attribute B. To specify a logical and, create a single resolution condition that contains both the attribute that precedes and the attribute that follows the attribute to which you want to assign the conflicting parsed value. To specify a logical or, create two separate resolution conditions; one resolution condition for the attribute that precedes the attribute to which you want to assign the parsed value and a second resolution condition for the attribute that follows the attribute to which you want to assign the parsed value.  Note Conflict resolutions are

the attribute that follows the attribute to which you want to assign the parsed value.  Note Conflict resolutions are not specific to each parsed value. After you define a resolution condition for the first instance of a specific type of conflict, you can ignore any additional conflict prompts that apply to that same type of conflict. In other words, after defining conflict resolution conditions for the color RED, when you assign the next color, BLACK, the Resolve Conflict dialog opens. You can choose to ignore the conflict and Cleansing Package Builder will apply the existing resolution conditions to BLACK. Parsing rules and confidence scores After classifying the values in an input string, Data Cleanse tries to apply each of the parsing rules in the cleansing package. A single input string can match more than one parsing rule. In the event that more than one parsing rule matches the input string, the rule with the higher confidence score is applied. In the event that more than one parsing rule matches the input string and the rules have equal confidence scores, Data Cleanse applies the first parsing rule in the rule order. You can affect which rule Data Cleanse applies in the following ways: Add a confidence booster to the confidence score Move the position of the rule up or down in the rule order (applies only to user-generated rules) 870 PUBLIC User Guide Cleansing Package Builder [PAGE 871] Confidence booster You can add a weight or confidence booster to the calculated confidence score in order to give a specific rule more or less weight compared to other similar rules. The booster may be a positive or

give a specific rule more or less weight compared to other similar rules. The booster may be a positive or negative integer. If you choose to include a confidence booster, it must be placed in the option line at the beginning of the Rule Action list, immediately following the output type and optional dual name indicator. The following examples of option lines show how user-defined weight can be added to the calculated confidence score. action = PAPER conf : 3; action = PERSON conf : 3; action = PERSON conf : -5; action = PERSON : D conf : 22; Scoring and computing confidence in person and firm cleansing packages For each rule that applies to an input string in the PERSON or FIRM categories, Data Cleanse calculates a confidence score. The terms PERSON parse and FIRM parse refer to the specific parser and sequential series of parsed and classified values in an input string. For PERSON rules, Data Cleanse uses a combination of two different, individual scores—the distance score and the look-up score. The distance score is calculated by using weights assigned to each of the parsed components. In contrast, the look-up score is calculated based on how different

using weights assigned to each of the parsed components. In contrast, the look-up score is calculated based on how different the parsed value in the input string is from the actual component value. Data Cleanse calculates the difference between these two scores and normalizes the result to a 100 point scale. For FIRM rules, Data Cleanse compares the number of values classified as FIRM words with the total number of parsed values in the input string, and normalizes the result to a 100 point scale. It then applies adjustments to the score when applicable: If a FIRM parse contains a FIRM_TERMINATOR parsed value, 50 points are added to the confidence score. If a FIRM parse does not use all available parsed values in the input string, the confidence score is halved. If the resulting confidence score is less than 20, the confidence score is reset to 20, the minimum allowable FIRM confidence score. If the resulting confidence score is greater than 100, the confidence score is reset to 100, the maximum allowable FIRM confidence score. After Data Cleanse has calculated the internal confidence score for each rule, it applies any additional confidence boosters that are specified in the parsing rules.

Ranking matching rules in person and firm cleansing packages After Data Cleanse has identified all matching rules and calculated final confidence scores, the rules are then ranked in descending order. User Guide Cleansing Package Builder PUBLIC 871 [PAGE 872] If the input string matches only PERSON rules and there is more than one PERSON rule with the same confidence score, Data Cleanse uses the rule that comes first in the rule order. Likewise, If the input string matches only FIRM rules and there is more than one FIRM rule with the same confidence score, Data Cleanse uses the rule that comes first in the rule order. PERSON and FIRM confidence scores are not directly comparable. If the input string matches both PERSON and FIRM rules, Data Cleanse determines which rule to use by using special tie-breaking criteria in the following order: If the PERSON parse contains a TITLE or is a dual name parse containing a PRENAME and none of the FIRM's parsed values are classified as FIRM_INITIATOR or FIRM_TERMINATOR, and the FIRM confidence score is not more than 40

the FIRM's parsed values are classified as FIRM_INITIATOR or FIRM_TERMINATOR, and the FIRM confidence score is not more than 40 greater than the PERSON confidence score, the PERSON parse is used. 2. If the FIRM confidence score is less than 100, the PERSON parse has no FIRM parsed values, the FIRM parse has no CONNECTOR parsed values, and there are no unused FIRM parsed values in the PERSON parse, the PERSON parse is used. 3. If the FIRM confidence score is greater than 50, the FIRM parse is used. 4. If the FIRM confidence score is greater than 10 and the PERSON confidence score is less than 20, the FIRM parse is used. 5. If there are unused FIRM parsed values found in the PERSON parse, the FIRM parse is used. If the PERSON confidence score is less than 34, the FIRM parse contains a CONNECTOR word, and the CONNECTOR word is used in the 3rd position or later, the FIRM parse is used. 8. The cleansed data is sent to output fields specified by the Data Services administrator or tester. The Data Cleanse transform follows a multi-step process: Breaks apart your input data into parsed values and classifies them. Finds which parsing rule or rules match each field in your data. Applies the parsing rule which has the highest confidence score. Outputs your cleansed data. Input data formats The uncleansed input data can be in one of the following input field formats: Discrete Multiline Hybrid In a discrete input field format the data is already its most distinct level. For example, a field containing only given names would be discrete, whereas a field containing a mixture of given name, middle name, and family name information would not be discrete, but rather multiline. In a multiline input field format the data is not consistently located in the same arrangement for all records. For example, a person and firm multiline input field might contain a person's

in the same arrangement for all records. For example, a person and firm multiline input field might contain a person's name in one record and a firm's name in another record. Records in a multiline input field for a paper product description might contain all or some of the following elements: part number, color, size, and weight. A hybrid format contains mixed data in which some fields are discrete and others are in a multiline format. 888 PUBLIC User Guide Cleansing Package Builder [PAGE 889] 6.11.1 Parse and classify input for person and firm cleansing packages The process used to break input data into chunks or tokens called parsed values and then classify them. The following information applies to person and firm cleansing packages. A slightly different process occurs for custom cleansing packages. The steps in the process are: Break input data [page 889] parsed values. 2. Combine contiguous parsed values [page 890]. 3. Classify parsed values [page 890]. 4. Gather parsed values [page 891] where possible to create larger values. 5. Combine compound values [page 892]. These classified parsed values can then be used by the rule-based parser. In a person and firm cleansing package, by default, data is broken based on the Parse data on whitespace and transitions between letters, numbers, script changes, or special characters parsing strategy. The input string is broken into individual values based on the following criteria: Leading spaces are skipped. Punctuation characters are identified as individual parsed values. Consecutive alphabetic characters are identified as a single parsed value. Consecutive numeric characters are identified as a single parsed value. Consecutive alphabetic characters that are OTHER_SCRIPT are identified as parsed values. Consecutive alphabetic characters that are East Asian scripts are identified as parsed values. About Odoo Online Book [PAGE 15] KAPITEL 2 Start with Odoo Online 2.1 Introduction Odoo (On Demand Open Object) is an open source suite of business applications; it became the world’s most downloa- ded and used business application software, with more than 5 million users worldwide. According to Wikipedia, Odoo is an all-in-one management software that offers a range of business applications that form a complete suite of enter- prise management applications. The Odoo solution is ideal for SMEs, but ﬁts both small and large companies alike. Odoo is an all-in-one business software capable of covering all business needs, including CRM, website/e-commerce, billing, accounting, manufacturing, warehouse, project management, and inventory, all seamlessly integrated. Tips: In 2005, Fabien Pinckaers, the Founder and CEO of Odoo, started to develop his ﬁrst software product,

seamlessly integrated. Tips: In 2005, Fabien Pinckaers, the Founder and CEO of Odoo, started to develop his ﬁrst software product, TinyERP. Later in the beginning of 2009 it was renamed to OpenERP, in May 2014, the company was renamed Odoo, a name that has no restrictions and can allow the company to grow in whichever direction. Odoo offers two different versions of the solution; Odoo Enterprise and Odoo Community Edition. The community edition is free to download and can be used anywhere. The Enterprise edition comes with many out of the box applica- tions, unlimited support software support, migration service. The Enterprise edition can be available as Odoo Online SaaS (Software as a Service) or on Odoo.sh or you can install on your private server too. The Odoo Online version is hosted on a cloud, and the ﬁrst app is offered for free for unlimited users. After the ﬁrst app, there is a ﬁxed monthly subscription fee for the number of apps installed and the number of users. The Community version is the open source version and available for free to use on your own server. Today, more and more companies are choosing to host their business application on an

to use on your own server. Today, more and more companies are choosing to host their business application on an Odoo online cloud platform, it is too costly for the companies to host their business application on local hardware. This approach requires not only a lot of capital to buy hardware and software licenses, but also creates a lot of responsibilities and risk in backing up data and ensuring stability of the business application. There are different kind of service sales: prepaid volume of hours/days (e.g. support contract), billing based on time and material (e.g. billing consulting hours) or a ﬁxed price contract (e.g. a project). Milestone invoicing can be used for expensive or large scale projects, with each milestone representing a clear sequence of work that will incrementally build up to the completion of the contract. For example, a marketing agency hired for a Kapitel 4. Sales & Invoicing [PAGE 85] Odoo Online Book, Utgåva 12.0 new product launch could break down a project into the following milestones, each of them considered as one service with a ﬁxed

launch could break down a project into the following milestones, each of them considered as one service with a ﬁxed price on the sale order : • Milestone 1 : Marketing strategy audit - 5 000 euros • Milestone 2 : Brand Identity - 10 000 euros • Milestone 3 : Campaign launch & PR - 8 500 euros In this case, an invoice will be sent to the customer each time a milestone will be successfully reached. That invoicing method is comfortable both for the company which is ensured to get a steady cash ﬂow throughout the project lifetime and for the client who can monitor the project’s progress and pay in several times. Observera: You can also use milestones to invoice percentages of the entire project. For example, for a million euros project, your company might require a 15% upfront payment, 30% at the midpoint and the balance at the contract conclusion. In that case, each payment will be considered as one milestone. Conﬁguration In order to sell services and to send invoices, you need to install the Sales application, from the Apps icon. [PAGE 90] Odoo Online Book, Utgåva 12.0 5.2 The Accounting behind Odoo This page summarises the way Odoo deals with typical accounts and transactions. 5.2.1 Double-entry bookkeeping Odoo automatically creates all the behind-the-scenes journal entries for each of your accounting transactions: customer invoices, point of sale order, expenses, inventory moves, etc. Odoo uses the rules of double-entry bookkeeping system: all journal entries are automatically balanced (sum of debits = sum of credits). 5.2.2 Accrual and Cash Basis Methods Odoo support both accrual and cash basis reporting. This allows you to report income / expense at the time transactions occur (i.e., accrual basis), or when payment is made or received (i.e., cash basis). 5.2.3 Multi-companies Odoo allows to manage several companies within the same database. Each company has its own chart of accounts and rules. You can get consolidation reports following your consolidation rules. Users can access several companies but always work in one company at a time. 5.2.4 Multi-currencies Every transaction is recorded in the default currency of the company. For transactions occurring in another currency,

For transactions occurring in another currency, Odoo stores both the value in the currency of the company and the value in the currency of the transaction. Odoo can generate currencies gains and losses after the reconciliation of the journal items. Currency rates are updated once a day using a yahoo.com online web-service. 5.2.5 International Standards Odoo accounting support more than 50 countries. The Odoo core accounting implement accounting standards that is common to all countries and speciﬁc modules exists per country for the speciﬁcities of the country like the chart of accounts, taxes, or bank interfaces. In particular, Odoo’s core accounting engine supports: • Anglo-Saxon Accounting (U.S., U.K.„ and other English-speaking countries including Ireland, Canada, Austra- lia, and New Zealand) where cost of good sold are reported when products are sold/delivered. • European accounting where expenses are accounted at the supplier bill. • Storno accounting (Italy) where refund invoices have negative credit/debit instead of a reverting the original journal items. • Odoo also have modules to comply with IFRS rules. This means, in order to produce goods tailored to customer requirements and provide faster deliveries, the enterprise must be closely linked to both suppliers and customers. In order to achieve this improved delivery performance, decreased lead times within the enterprise and improved efficiency and effectiveness, manufacturers need to have efficient planning and control systems that enable very good synchronization and planning in all the processes of the organization. Also, it requires a strong integration across the value chain. Hence, there is a need for a standard software package, which equips the enterprise with the necessary capabilities to integrate and synchronize the isolated functions into streamlined business processes in order to gain a competitive edge in the volatile business environment. Most organisations across the world have realised that in a rapidly changing environment, it is impossible to create and maintain a custom-designed software package, which will cater to all their requirements, and be up-to-date. Realising the requirement of user organisations, some of the leading software companies have designed Enterprise Resource Planning software, which offers an integrated software solution to all the functions of an organisation. Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) is the latest high-end solution, information technology has lent to business applications. The ERP solutions seek to streamline and integrate operation processes and information flows in the company to synergise the resources of an organisation namely men, material, money and machine through information. Initially implementation of an ERP package was possible only for large multi nationals and infrastructure companies due to high cost. Today, many companies in India have gone in for implementation of ERP. It organizes and integrates operation processes and information flows to make optimum use of resources such as men, material, money and machine. ERP is a global, tightly integrated closed loop business solution package and is multifaceted. In simple words, Enterprise resource planning promises one database, one application, and one user interface for the entire enterprise, where once disparate systems ruled manufacturing, distribution, finance and sales. Taking information from every function it is a tool that assists employees and managers plan, monitor and control the entire business. A modern ERP system enhances a manufacturer ability to accurately schedule production, fully utilize capacity, reduce inventory, and meet promised shipping dates. The new era of PC, advent of client server technology and scalable Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMS), all have contributed for the ease of deployment of ERP systems. Most of the ERP systems exploit the power of Three Tier Client Server Architecture. In a client server environment, the server stores the data, maintaining its integrity and consistency and processes the requests of the user from the client desktops. The load of data processing and application logic is divided between the server and the client. The three-tier architecture adds a middle stratum, embodying

processing and application logic is divided between the server and the client. The three-tier architecture adds a middle stratum, embodying all application logic and the business rules that are not part of the application, enforcing appropriate validation checks. It is assumed that the companies implementing ERP solutions have multiple locations of operation and control. Hence, the online data transfer has to be done across locations. To facilitate these transactions, the other important enabling technologies for ERP systems are Workflow, Work group, Group Ware, Electronic Data Interchange (EDI), Internet, Intranet, Data warehousing, etc. 7.1.3 ERP Characteristics : An ERP system is not only the integration of various organization processes. Here, dramatic achievement means to achieve 80% or 90% reduction (in say, delivery time, work in progress or rejection rate) and not just 5%, 10% reduction. This is possible only by making major improvements and breakthroughs, and not small incremental changes (like those in Total Quality Management (TQM) or suggestion schemes). In a nutshell, a “cleansiate approach” of BPR says that “Whatever you were doing in the past is all wrong”, do not get biased by it or reassemble you new system to redesign it afresh. Fundamental rethinking means asking the question “why do you do what you do”, thereby eliminating business process altogether if it does not add any value to the customer. There is no point in simplifying or automating a business process which does not add any value to the customer. At its simplest level, ERP is a set of best practices for performing the various duties in the departments of your company, including in finance, manufacturing and the warehouse. To get the most from the software, you have to get people inside your company to adopt the work methods outlined in the software. If the people in the different departments that will use ERP don’t agree that the work methods embedded in the software are better than the ones they currently use, they will resist using the software or will want IT to change the software to match the ways they currently do things. This is where ERP projects break down. Political fights erupt over how or even whether the software will be installed. IT gets bogged down in long, expensive customisation efforts to modify the ERP software to fit with powerful business barons’ wishes. Customisations make the software more unstable and harder to maintain when it finally does come to life. Because ERP covers so much of what a business does, a failure in the software can bring a company to a halt, literally.

so much of what a business does, a failure in the software can bring a company to a halt, literally. The mistake companies make is assuming that changing people’s habits will be easier than customising the software. It’s not. Getting people inside your company to use the software to improve the ways they do their jobs is by far the harder challenge. If people are resistant to change, then the ERP project is more likely to fail. 7.6 How does ERP Fit with e-commerce? ERP vendors were not prepared for the onslaught of e-commerce. ERP is complex and not intended for public consumption. It assumes that the only people handling order information will be your employees, who are highly trained and comfortable with the tech jargon embedded in the software. But now customers and suppliers are demanding access to the same information your employees get through the ERP system - things such as order status, inventory levels and invoice reconciliation, except they want to get all this information simply, without all the ERP software jargon, through your website. E-commerce means IT departments need to build two new channels of access into ERP systems, one for customers (otherwise known as business-to-consumer)

IT departments need to build two new channels of access into ERP systems, one for customers (otherwise known as business-to-consumer) and one for suppliers and partners (business-to-business). These two audiences want two different types of information from your ERP system. Consumers want order status and billing information, and suppliers and partners want just about everything else. The bottom line, however, is those companies with e-commerce ambitions face a lot of hard integration work to make their ERP systems available over the Web.
